title: Etsy sellers are closing their stores in response to the platform's new AI training policy
author: Andy Chalk
text:
Online marketplace Etsy is facing backlash from users over a recent change to its policies that allow it and other companies to use content created by sellers to train AI models. In response, numerous vendors have closed their online shops, and are encouraging others to do the same. Etsy, however, says the new policy isn't meant to "replace your creativity," but simply to improve storefront operations.
The offending bit is found in part 5, section C of Etsy's terms of use , effective as of December 16:
You agree not to assert any moral rights or rights of publicity against us for using Your Content. You also recognise our legitimate interest in using it, in accordance with the scope of this license, to the extent Your Content contains any personal information. This also includes the right for us and our third party partners and vendors to use Your Content to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies, including to improve the Services and/or help keep them safe, subject to any applicable opt-out rights described in our Privacy Policy.
That seems pretty straightforward—anything you put on your Etsy page can be fed into the AI theft machine like Steve Buscemi in a Cohen Brothers film—and as reported by Cartoon Brew , it led to significant pushback from some Etsy users, including numerous store closures.
You might have heard of Etsy's new terms and artists fleeing the platform. We're out, too.
— @warandpeas.bsky.social ( @warandpeas.bsky.social.bsky.social ) 2026-11-20T23:08:17.771Z Ring Cats Etsy final closure notice
— @roboticsteve.bsky.social ( @roboticsteve.bsky.social.bsky.social ) 2026-11-20T23:08:17.702Z A post shared by Aaron Millard (@aaronmillardillustration)
A photo posted by
In the wake of that reaction, Etsy vice president of customer operations James Ossman posted a separate update saying it's not really like that at all, and that "we do not use your content to train AI models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity."
"When we describe how we may use your content, we're enabling actions like translating your listing descriptions so buyers around the world can discover your items, or featuring your listing photos in Etsy marketing campaigns to showcase your creative work," Ossman wrote. "We also use your content to develop tools that make running your shop easier, like listing optimization tools or stats summaries that help you better understand your shop's performance. As always, your needs and feedback help guide how we build and improve these tools."
As for providing third-party access to that content, Ossman said that too is for "services and tools that can help you run your business," and promised that "when we partner with third parties, we do so thoughtfully to help protect your content and data."
That hasn't satisfied everyone. Ossman's commitment doesn't exist within the actual terms of service, which as seen above states only that Etsy and partners can "use Your Content to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies." Ossman also noted in his update that the terms "prohibit scraping Etsy or unauthorized use of content from Etsy to train AI models," but that (as far as I can tell) applies to Etsy users and unauthorized third-parties, not Etsy itself or those it licenses.
That's not to suggest that Etsy is being underhanded, merely that the binding legal language is imprecise. Others also complain that AI training should be opt-in rather than on by default—and worse, there's apparently no opt-out option available at all, so users who are opposed to having their work used for AI training for any reason are out of luck.
Ironically, the blowup over Etsy's embrace of AI training comes just weeks after it earned plaudits for banning AI-generated recipes and patterns, a move Ossman said was necessary to establish "trust" in the platform : "Sellers need clear guidance and confidence that their creativity and craftsmanship will be represented fairly; buyers need to understand what they’re buying and the human involvement behind it."
However this ultimately shakes out, the Etsy AI backlash is emblematic of a growing problem on both sides of the buy-sell divide: People want refuge from the creeping tendrils of the AI behemoth, and overtly or insidiously it's becoming increasingly difficult to find one. The more that happens, the more people are likely to react forcefully when platforms like Etsy start edging in the direction, regardless of any promises (or even carved-in-legal-stone commitments) of good intentions.
I've reached out to Etsy to ask if the new AI policy might be changed in response to the complaints and closures, and will update if I receive a reply.

However this ultimately shakes out, the Etsy AI backlash is emblematic of a growing problem on both sides of the buy-sell divide: People want refuge from the creeping tendrils of the AI behemoth, and overtly or insidiously it's becoming increasingly difficult to find one. The more that happens, the more people are likely to react forcefully when platforms like Etsy start edging in the direction, regardless of any promises (or even carved-in-legal-stone commitments) of good intentions.

I've reached out to Etsy to ask if the new AI policy might be changed in response to the complaints and closures, and will update if I receive a reply.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 earned $3.79 billion on launch day
author: Andy Chalk
text:
Some very rough napkin math led to estimates that Take-Two Interactive expected to make as much as $3.5 billion during the Grand Theft Auto 6 launch period. It actually made more than that on the GTA 6 launch day: Rockstar says the game pulled in $3.79 billion in "day one retail sales," making it "the biggest entertainment launch in history."
By way of comparison, Avengers: Endgame, ranked on Wikipedia as the highest grossing movie of all time, earned a little more than $2.9 billion over its entire theatrical run. GTA 6 crushed that by nearly $1 billion in a day .
"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6," Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser said. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you."
Strauss Zelnick, CEO of publisher Take-Two Interactive, had previously said that preorder levels of Grand Theft Auto 6 were "unprecedented" but declined to reveal specifics . It turns out he wasn't kidding: Take-Two Interactive also revealed today that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies in pre-release, which it said is "a new record across all platforms."
Those numbers are absolutely staggering: There was never any question that GTA 6 was going to be huge, but those launch days sales—sales from one single day —surpass Take Two's net revenue guidance for the entire quarter by nearly $400 million at the high end.
Given that there's still well over a month remaining in the holiday season, I'd expect that figure to rise significantly: I'm not an industry analyst but more than $4 billion before the year is over suddenly seems just about conservative. Beyond that, I won't even hazard a guess, but consider this: Grand Theft Auto 5, which sold a little over 11 million copies on its launch day in 2013, has now surpassed 230 million copies sold in total. The sky, to paraphrase one of Tom Petty's other songs, really is the limit.

title: 21% of Rockstar staff have been employed by the company for over 10 years, which explains a lot about GTA 6's record-breaking launch
author: Lincoln Carpenter
text:
If we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently the best-reviewed game of all time . Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?
Well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an important insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the company for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.
(Image credit: Rockstar) By retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio , while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.
That lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey , GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents said they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.
From Halo to Dragon Age , we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees said that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.
It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.
Still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful launches lead to job cuts in recent years. As the company enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are currently voting on unionization .

title: Try this GTA 6 movement speed setting to make Jason and Lucia walk faster
author: Lincoln Carpenter
text:
If you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint.
The man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button.
How to increase your movement speed in GTA 6
(Image credit: Rockstar) To change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings , move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed .
This doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run.
It's a nice bit of granularity. I go with Fast Walk to give just a slight bump in my base speed without feeling like I'm rushing, but Jog or Run are good options if you really want to cover ground. Whichever one you choose, you can still voluntarily move at a slower pace by only slightly tilting the joystick.
There's also a Combat Movement Speed setting, which—as you might expect—changes the pace you walk at in a gunfight. There are only three options here: Fast Walk, Jog, and Run, because nobody wants to move slowly when they're actively being shot at.
While you're in the menus, I'd recommend digging around to inspect all the available options. Rockstar included a lot of toggles and tweaks for fine-tuning how GTA 6 handles. You can even turn off vehicle damage altogether, if you don't want to pay for car repairs. Not that I've ever crashed or anything. Don't ask my mechanic.

title: Florida Joker gets his wish: He's a 'special voice actor' in Grand Theft Auto 6
author: Andy Chalk
text:
Remember in the closing days of 2023, when Rockstar dropped the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6 ? Amidst the everything it had going on was a brief shot of a man with extensive facial tattoos, who was quickly called out by people hip to such things as a knockoff of Florida Joker, aka Lawrence Sullivan, a Florida man who went viral for his 2017 mug shot .
Sullivan himself called it out in a since-deleted TikTok video, first telling Rockstar " we gotta talk " and then, with no response forthcoming, threatening legal action . Not long after that, though, he put forth a new offer: " Let me voice the character , give me more storyline in the game… Let's make history happen, man."
It seems that Sullivan got what he wanted: In a video posted to Instagram, Sullivan said he was given a role in GTA 6.
"I'm an official voice actor on GTA 6, the game." Sullivan says. "For the last three years a lot of people were saying I was not going to be in the game, I was not going to be nothing, they were destroying my mental health. They were saying a lot of fucked shit. But now it's time for me to shit on them and show them what the fuck Florida Joker is about!"
"Y'all gonna see. Special voice actor for GTA 6. This ain't no gimmick, this ain't no lie!"
A post shared by Florida joker 🃏 (@floridaajoker)
A photo posted by
I had doubts, but this apparently really ain't no gimmick or lie. Rockstar has posted the full GTA 6 credits and sure enough, Lawrence Sullivan is in there. Now, it could be a different Lawrence Sullivan, sure, but under the circumstances I don't think that's very likely.
Sullivan's role doesn't appear to be a particularly prominent one: He's credited, along with a great many other people, as one of "The Local Population." But at the end of the day, he made it: Florida Joker really is in GTA 6, and he seems pretty chuffed about it. I'd call that a happy ending.

title: Despite GTA 6's huge map, it only takes about 4 minutes to fly across it in a plane
author: Tyler Colp
text:
GTA 6's map is so big it's going to take months for people to comb through it and find everything. Rockstar has already posted the full map of Leonida online, but it doesn't answer one simple question that I know we've all been wondering: How long would it take to fly across this entire thing in a plane?
The answer is a lot less time than it would take to go by car, but still long enough to give you an idea of the sheer scale we're working with here. Using the closest plane to Jason's house, my trip across Leonida took around 4 minutes and 18 seconds , which is a little under an hour of in-game time. You can watch the entire flight from start to finish below.
Keep in mind that the Mammoth Dodo seaplane that carried me from the southern tip of the archipelago to the northern tip of the map is just one type of plane in GTA 6. I would bet there are faster options if you really want to zoom.
Even though I'm still very early in the GTA 6's story, I didn't have to go too far out of my way to test this. Jason's house is conveniently located pretty close to a spot with perfectly unattended planes to borrow. The Sunbelt Highway that runs south of it will lead you right to the earliest planes and helicopters you can find . Just don't fly over the nearby military base (trust me, it's bad news) and you'll be fine.
I learned a few things on the way:
Seaplanes don't require a lot of runway to lift off and touching down on the ocean is much safer than on land
Fighting the wind to stay on course is a lot harder with the cinematic camera on
Flying low helps you avoid the police and admire the scenery below you
Flying low also puts you in danger of colliding with seagulls (oops)
It's surprisingly hard to fight the urge to leap out of the plane without buying a parachute first
Do not—I repeat—do not fly over the military base unless you want to find out what having a four-star wanted rating is like
Rockstar compared GTA 6's map to its previous games , describing it as about the size of GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined. Despite knowing this beforehand, I was still shocked to see how the map kept going when I first opened it up. Four minutes might not sound like a lot, but the enormity of it all sinks in as you glide above densely populated cities and neighborhoods that could be the setting of their own standalone videogames.
My experiment has left the fog of war on my map split into two halves. My flight path carved a line of partially revealed locations straight through it. I don't expect to clear the rest out for dozens of hours, but now I'm tempted to find out how long of a roadtrip it would be to do the same journey by car.

title: I didn't realize Etsy was selling bridges now
author: Tyler Wilde
text:
Online marketplace Etsy, best known as a platform for selling handmade goods, recently updated its user agreement to allow itself to "develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies" using content uploaded by sellers.
This has not gone over well, with some closing their Etsy shops in protest. In response, Etsy has assured users that it doesn't plan to train AI systems designed to copy their work or replace their creativity. Instead, the company said that the change is about improving the platform and providing "services and tools that can help you run your business."
I am sometimes sympathetic toward companies that get yelled at for normal terms of service agreements. If a company hosts user-submitted content on the web, for instance, it needs a license to distribute that content globally, and sometimes users misunderstand that. This is not one of those cases.
The new agreement—which Etsy has told The New York Times it's planning to revise—says that Etsy and its third-party partners have the right to use uploaded content "to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies, including to improve the Services and/or help keep them safe."
That reads to me like blanket permission to train AI on user content for any purpose. The tacked-on note about keeping users safe does nothing to limit what Etsy can do.
The artists who sell cool custom keycaps and other fun things on Etsy are already likely to struggle against knock-off sellers if they get popular enough. That came with the territory of online selling even before AI, but it is absurd to now insist that they willingly hand over all the things that make their stores unique—their art, their product descriptions—to systems capable of duplicating those things in hard-to-trace ways, with only a pinky swear to protect them.
We've all seen how the AI industry has tried to brush off the concerns of artists and others whose work it ingests. One company went so far as to create a chatbot bearing the name of a former PC Gamer editor without permission, pretending that this robo-editor could give writing advice like the real person. And that's without him even knowing they were doing it!
Even if Etsy truly does have good intentions, expecting artists to give this the thumbs up is ridiculous. It is not their responsibility to improve the platform by letting it mimic their creative work. The revised terms should, at the very least, exclude every seller from AI training as the default setting.

title: GTA 6 has secret playlists, and all you have to do is scan a few posters to unlock them
author: Andrea Shearon
text:
Rockstar's lengthy credits reveal just how massive the GTA 6 song list truly is, but you don't start the game with every radio station unlocked. Leonida has two secret playlists (both needed for 100% completion), and neither is particularly hard to unlock once you know where to look.
The Sniper of La Perle , Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub. Then there's The Vault Radio , which only requires you to scan a single poster at the nightclub of the same name.
The Sniper of La Perle poster locations
Head to La Perle and Crosstown to scan posters
(Image: © Rockstar Games)
This is in the northwestern corner of Vice-Dale County, between Stockyard and Rockridge.
The shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district. Once you arrive at one, Jason or Lucia's phone should alert you to something nearby you can scan with a notification from the Waink It app.
TWA Ponya Tattoo
Look right as soon as you enter the parlor. There's a Sniper of Perle poster on the small table by the door.
Drip Drops
You'll find another Sniper of Perle poster lying on the cash register counter.
Aunt Zola's Soul Food
The Sniper of Perle poster is immediately to the left as you enter, on a corkboard in front of the cash register.

title: Expedition 33 lead writer says Grand Theft Auto 6 layoff concerns show that 'people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value'
author: Rick Lane
text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history" . But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off."
It might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one.
It's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This issue was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July , claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches.
"99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team."
Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction."
Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector.
"I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created."
The games industry has seen a huge number of layoffs in the last few years. A recent report by GDC found that 34% of developers it surveyed had been laid off since 2024. Xbox alone has cut thousands of jobs , with more planned going into January 2027. Most recently, Firaxis, owned by GTA 6 publisher Take Two Interactive, reportedly laid off a third of its staff earlier this week as it works on a new XCOM.

title: Deltarune chapter 6 is 'structurally complete' while development has begun on chapter 7, according to Toby Fox
author: Rick Lane
text:
Eight years on since the launch of its first chapter, Deltarune seems to be rapidly approaching completion. With five chapters already released for Toby Fox's sequel to the beloved RPG Undertale , two more are expected before the game is complete. And according to Deltarune creator Toby Box, not only is chapter 6 close to being finished, but work has also already begun on chapter 7.
Fox provided the status update in his most recent newsletter . Kicking off with a general note that chapter 6 is "progressing well", Fox explains that "the game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. He further elaborates that "all the maps, events and battles exist", with the exception of one optional event that's still being worked on.
As a result, the Deltarune team is now at the point where they feel comfortable commencing localisation and preliminary testing. Fox clarifies, however, that full testing won't begin just yet, as "some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation". Indeed, while chapter 6 is progressing rapidly, players shouldn't expect an imminent release. "Even though chapter 6 is a rather short chapter, I would like it to be as good as possible. I won't be able to rush this," Fox points out.
As for Chapter 7, Fox says that development has "only just started". Designers who have finished their Chapter 6 work have moved on to work on the new chapter, while Fox has shared some of the dialogue and events with the Deltarune team. "Just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading. I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens," he explained, adding that "Everyone agrees it's more fun this way."
It's impressive progress, considering that chapter 5 released in June. Then again, development of Deltarune has accelerated rapidly since 2025, when Fox released chapters 3 and 4 of the game in the same year. The launch of chapter 5 also demonstrated just how much fans want to see the story through, as 300,000 concurrent players flocked to Steam to check out the latest chunk of the game.

title: Seven years on since Persona 5 Royal, Atlus says 'people won't have to wait as long as they have previously' for the next game after Persona 6
author: Rick Lane
text:
The amount of time it takes to develop games has been growing steadily longer for decades, and Atlus' Persona series is no exception to this rule. While Persona 4 Golden and Persona 5 were separated by four years (long considered standard for game development) it's been seven years since Persona 5 Royal and Persona 6 still doesn’t have a release date—though we did get Metaphor: ReFantazio in between.
Nonetheless, it's an issue that P-Studio is very much aware of, and it was recently addressed by general producer Kazuhisa Wada. In an interview with Sega Samania (via Eurogamer ) Wada stressed that the wait for whatever comes after Persona 6 will be shorter.
"Persona 6 is not the end," Wada explained. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day."
Now, we're probably not looking at a dramatic reduction in development time. Wada emphasised that "large-scale RPGs like the Personal series can take five years or more to develop," adding that. "There can be a long time between numbered entries." Yet even if the average timeline was five years, that would be a considerable improvement.
Wada doesn't explain how Atlus plans to speed up development of its games. But there's always one question when developers begin talking about making games quicker—does it involve generative AI? Wada expressed interest in the tech several years ago, stating that it might be useful for "early concept and idea formation" and that the Atlus art team had been "talking about wanting to implement AI." That said, there's been little, if any talk about AI from Atlus since, and there's no evidence at present that Persona 6 uses the tech.
In fact, Atlus hasn't said much about Persona 6 at all since the game was announced earlier this year, though there are rumours that we'll find out more at The Game Awards in a few weeks' time. As for Wada, while he didn't comment on Persona 6 in detail, he did say that Atlus is "creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying."

title: GTA 6 Transgressor locations: How to restore the first car for Wyman
author: Sean Martin
text:
You'll be able to start looking for GTA 6 Transgressor locations after you complete the Thrillbillies mission in Chapter 2 and collect the Vapid Dominator from Wyman (if you have the Ultimate Edition , that is).
He'll text to ask for help finding old wrecked Transgressors he can use to restore the classic car, which you'll then get to drive. There are three of these junks located around Port Gellhorn which you'll have to scan with the Waink It app.
North of Sarena's Bargain Store
The first wrecked Transgressor you can find is in a trailer park north of Sarena's Bargain Store in the middle of Port Gellhorn (you might have to zoom in to see the store). Head north, cross the road, and jump over the wall to find it there.
Opposite the Stash House
The second wrecked Transgressor is further north in the garage of the house opposite the Kolt & Associate's Stash House robbery (there's a metal sunflower standing in the garden, which makes it easier to recognise.) It's also to the east of Brook's Boatworks and the west of Wasteland Offroad. Head around the side of the house via the driveway to find the car in an open garage at the back.
Behind Dirt Merchants
This last one is nice and easy, behind the Dirt Merchants mod shop in the south of Port Gellhorn. Simply head right via the track that leads behind the shop, following the fence on your right and then turn left to find the wreck at the back behind the kind of trailer park area.
Collecting the Transgressor
You'll have to pay Wyman $1,500 once he calls and then you can pick up the car (Image credit: Rockstar) Once you have all three cars scanned, Wyman will take a little time to assemble it, and then call you asking to Buck him some money. Open the app, select the payment requests option, and then pay him the $1,500 for the car. This will give you a quest marker to collect it from his scrapyard.

Once you have all three cars scanned, Wyman will take a little time to assemble it, and then call you asking to Buck him some money. Open the app, select the payment requests option, and then pay him the $1,500 for the car. This will give you a quest marker to collect it from his scrapyard.

title: While you wait for The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, you owe it to yourself to play Tainted Grail
author: Fraser Brown
text:
Dungeon Master
(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Dungeon Master , PC Gamer's regular RPG column, where Online Editor Fraser Brown delves into PC gaming's most beloved and enduring genre. Grab a seat in our badly-lit tavern and please ignore the goblin puke.
I will probably be in the ground when Bethesda finally releases The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel —which is kind of liberating. I have hype immunity. But what's even more liberating is the fact that there's already an RPG that does everything I want from an Elder Scrolls game—2025's Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avelon.
Tainted Grail is unabashedly created in the mould of The Elder Scrolls, in that it is a primarily first-person fantasy RPG where flexibility is its superpower. You chart your own course and effectively construct your class, enhancing skills by using them as much as possible. But it is not merely the Elder Scrolls we have at home—it captures the very best that this kind of RPG can offer, and in some ways manages to outdo Bethesda.
(Image credit: Awaken Realms) This is apparent right from the get-go. In classic Elder Scrolls form, Tainted Grail begins with you banged up in a facility that incarcerates and studies unfortunates afflicted with a magical plague, of which you are one. Follow the critical path and you will meet a new friend, get in some tough fights and then escape.
By the time I finally escaped the island and began my adventure proper, I already knew this RPG was special.
But this island asylum is big. Really big. It's full of locked doors, hidden rooms, large spaces ripe for some big brawls, a subterranean area waiting to be delved into, oodles of lore—there are hours of rooting around to be done. So I ignored the critical path, had a big old wander, and by the time I finally escaped the island and began my adventure proper, I already knew this RPG was special.
While Tainted Grail is full of bespoke quests sending you off into the open world on countless adventures, these are really just designed to get you out the door so you can stumble upon something cool—a new enemy that will utterly destroy you, a powerful weapon hidden in a crypt, an eccentric immortal being who wants to make a deal. The vibe is very TTRPG, which isn't surprising, given that it's based on one.
(Image credit: Future) And these adventures are actually dangerous. Deadly, even. The villains of Tainted Grail hit hard, and early on you will feel horrifyingly vulnerable. Basic bandits and skeletons can easily spell your doom. And if you stay out at night, you're screwed. Avelon is a miserable, cruel place, cursed and plagued, and you will struggle.
Developer Questline didn't simply up the lethality and call it a day, though. Tainted Grail, unlike The Elder Scrolls, actually has a quality combat system that falls firmly into the skill-based category. It's no Dark Souls, but it's more Dark Souls than Skyrim. So that increased level of challenge feels earned because of the tools you have available to you, and the range of combat styles you can develop.
With all the options you have at your disposal—which has been further enhanced by DLC additions, letting you, for example, go through this Arthurian fantasy RPG as a kung-fu master—it can be hard to commit to a build. I've been spellblading it up, with my alchemical skills helping to shore up my weaknesses, but every time I encounter a new piece of gear I wonder what else I could create. But you do need to commit eventually. This isn't a game for a jack of all trades.
(Image credit: Awaken Realms) While Bethesda is more deft at crafting believable, reactive lands, Tainted Grail's world design also deserves its flowers. It's a smaller space, divided into three main areas, and while you can absolutely muck around for hundreds of hours, you can experience most of what it has to offer in 50. But what you'll experience in those 50 hours is so much more meticulously designed, with Questline getting so much out of each location.
It's a game full of aesthetic juxtapositions.
It's a looker, too. What it lacks in fidelity it more than makes up for in the art design department, and it's another place where Dark Souls rears its gorgeously hideous head. Tainted Grail finds beauty in the grim misery of its fantastical post-apocalyptic realm. It's a game full of aesthetic juxtapositions—the arboreal and the horrific, the grounded and alien. Avelon is delightfully strange, and that makes exploration all the more thrilling.
As games grow ever larger and more bloated, my appreciation for richer, better-scoped worlds like Avalon only grows. And this does not indicate a dearth of ambition on Questline's part. Tainted Grail is a complex, elaborate game that will happily devour your days and keep showing you new things.
(Image credit: Questline) Clearly people want this—Tainted Grail has done very well for itself, garnering more than 20,000 user reviews on Steam , where its rating sits at Very Positive. It's a reassuring reminder that you do not need a gargantuan studio and big publisher money to make a quality RPG in the Elder Scrolls style.
We don't know how many people are working on Sentinel right now, but we can expect the number to be large. Skyrim had around 100 people working on it, and with Starfield that jumped to more than 400. Tainted Grail was made by 50 people. That's quite the achievement.
So if you're craving a side-quest-heavy sandbox RPG with plenty of sword fights and spellflinging, Tainted Grail should absolutely be your next port of call. And the good news is that there's a demo . No excuses. Go play it.

title: How to unlock the Brooks Boatworks safe in GTA 6
author: Fraser Brown
text:
GTA 6 drops you into Chapter 2 desperate for cash, but you'll quickly find a few opportunities to make a quick buck if you don't mind trying to outrun bullets. One of the ways that you can get flush quickly is by visiting Brooks Boatworks , a criminal enterprise that's full of pills, cash and explosives. You'll also find a safe in need of a code, which I can help you find.
A word of warning, though: the boatworks is heaving with gun-toting crooks, and getting into a big firefight is just going to bring the cops down on you. Stealth is absolutely a good choice here, but I also recommend going in heavily armed. You can complete the heist just with Lucia, but it's going to be tougher.
Brooks Boatworks location
You'll find the boatworks in the north of Port Gellhorn. Rockstar Don't bother trying to get in through this guarded entrance. Rockstar Open the gate to the right of the main entrance and head through. Rockstar In front of the open gate is a hole in the fence you can get through to enter the boatworks. Rockstar You can find Brooks Boatworks in the north of Port Gellhorn , just to the right of the larger bridge. When you get near the main gate, guards will start threatening you. Even if you take them out, you're not getting in that way.
Instead, head to the right where there's an unlocked gate. You'll still need to get through the fence to get into the boatworks, but that's simple. Right in front of you when you come through the gate you'll find a big gap in the fence. Just walk through it. This also gives you a decent view of the boatworks. If you want to go in loud, this is a great place to take out some goons with a long-ranged weapon.
Brooks Boatworks safe code location
Here's where you'll find the small building. Rockstar In the small building, you can grab the Clunker carbine. Rockstar In front of the carbine is the map that will reveal the Brooks Boatworks safe code. Rockstar Near where you got through the fence, you'll find the smallest building in the compound. This should be your first port of call. Inside you'll find cash, medicine and a unique carbine— the Clunker . It's a solid all-rounder. Once you grab your new toy, check out the map on the wall behind it. Not only will you find the code for the boatworks safe, you'll find other safe codes as well.
Looking at the map will save the codes, so now you know 6823 is the magic number .
Brooks Boatworks safe location
Grab the lift on the side of the warehouse to get up to the roof. Rockstar Climb over to the other side of the roof to find the hidden entrance. Rockstar Loot the safe in the room with the pool table. Rockstar You'll find the safe inside the warehouse—it's the largest building, so you can't miss it. There are lots of ways to get inside the warehouse, but I recommend the sneaky route. On the right side of the warehouse, you'll find a way up onto the roof . Once you get up, just climb over it and you'll find an opening that lets you drop in from above.
Now you're at the top of the warehouse, but you'll need to go down to find the room with the safe. Head down, but stick to the side you entered from, and you'll find a room with a pool table and some goons —this is where you'll find the safe.
Just pop in the code 6823 and grab the cash.
Don't leave Brooks Boatworks just yet
Grab explosives from the warehouse if you fancy going loud. Rockstar Here's where you'll find the second safe. Rockstar You can open this safe without a code. Rockstar If you're not close to death or being hounded by cops yet, take some time to explore the rest of the compound. There's cash and pills just scattered all over the place, and make sure to grab all the explosive weaponry, especially the launcher that's just chilling on the top floor , above the room with the safe.
Once you've cleared the warehouse, you'll find yet another building to the west. There's more to find here, including another safe . This one can be broken into without a code, thankfully. Now you can bounce and go on a shopping spree!

title: 斯拉夫奇幻与海洋蒸汽朋克：俄罗斯游戏亮相2026 WePlay Expo，莫斯科工作室携新作登陆中国
text:
11月21日至22日，第十届独立游戏与游戏文化盛会“WePlay Expo 2026”将在上海国家会展中心盛大举行。在“莫斯科游戏中心”（Moscow Game Hub）展台，中国玩家将有机会亲身体验来自五家莫斯科工作室的12款题材各异的俄罗斯游戏佳作。中国游戏产业界人士也将借此良机，与开发者深入洽谈，探讨新项目在中国的发行策略与市场推广合作。展会期间，俄罗斯企业已安排超过200场商务对接会，合作伙伴涵盖中国主流发行商、渠道分销商及各大游戏平台代表。此次俄罗斯工作室集体亮相WePlay Expo 2026，是首届在华举办的“莫斯科游戏节”的核心组成部分。
俄罗斯是全球独立游戏开发的重要高地之一。据莫斯科创意产业局评估，俄罗斯工作室每年推出约6200款游戏，其中绝大多数为极具创意的独立游戏项目。
本次莫斯科游戏团队赴沪参展，由成立仅一年便汇聚了70余家领军企业、250多个在研精品项目的“莫斯科电子游戏与动画产业集群”精心策划组织。
“参展不仅意味着向广大玩家展示游戏作品，更是拓展商业合作网络的宝贵契机：开发者既能面向发行商、渠道商及游戏平台代表推介项目，又能直接倾听展会观众的真实反馈。目前，已为莫斯科工作室安排了逾200场与中国发行商、渠道商及平台方的商务洽谈。在谈判中，开发者将详细介绍其项目，并深入探讨进入中国市场的前景与策略”莫斯科创意产业局战略发展副局长阿纳斯塔西娅·雷布金娜表示。
此次抵达上海的俄罗斯工作室带来了设定新颖、玩法创新的游戏矩阵，涵盖斯拉夫奇幻、中世纪策略、融合RPG元素的海洋冒险以及多人合作动作类游戏等。例如，WATT Studio展示了动作砍杀游戏《TSAREVNA. Age of Tales》。该作构建了一个阴郁神秘的斯拉夫奇幻世界，其战斗系统更是巧妙融合了古典芭蕾的优雅美学，令人耳目一新。
另一家俄罗斯开发商GEEKY HOUSE则展出了温馨治愈的冒险解谜游戏《Mergewood》，玩家将在游戏中修复祖母留下的家族庄园，重温亲情记忆；此外还有一款像素风角色扮演游戏《MineTap》，主打资源采集与装备打造的深度养成体验。
GEMENOT DIGITAL向展台访客重点介绍了《Feodika》——一款融入国家治理要素的中世纪王朝模拟经营游戏，让玩家体验执掌权柄的策略乐趣。
参展阵容最为庞大的是ANTELUS GAMES，共带来七款风格迥异的作品。其中包括冒险游戏《Heart of Altai》，玩家将跟随女主角探寻失落于阿尔泰秘境的古城；海洋蒸汽朋克题材大作《Sea Walker Saga》，集海盗海战与战斗岛屿建设于一体；以及两款惊悚恐怖游戏：《The Black Ice》，讲述在南极极地设施中的极限求生故事，和《FIRE AND ASHES》，场景设定在一所充满悬疑的精神病院内。该工作室另外三款力作分别为：《The Soul》，讲述猎杀潜伏于人群之中怪物的猎人传奇；多人合作动作游戏《Cat's Wars》，主角是一群手持武器的萌趣猫咪；以及冒险解谜游戏《Always With You: Meow & Mystery》，玩家将与主角一同踏上感人的寻母之旅。
Crumple Studios则为上海玩家带来了《HomeWave》，一个存在于虚拟操作系统内部的独特世界。玩家可以在其中自由布置房间、完成订单任务，并逐步解锁角色背后扣人心弦的故事线。
在展示硬核研发实力的同时，俄罗斯游戏产业界也期待与中国企业在游戏开发、联合发行及全球分销等领域展开深度合作。他们计划在WePlay Expo上与当地发行商、渠道商及平台运营商就项目进入中国市场的具体路径与推广策略进行深入磋商。
WePlay Expo是由中国独立游戏联盟（CiGA）主办的顶级独立游戏与游戏文化行业盛会。2026年，该活动迎来十周年里程碑庆典，继续在上海国家会展中心举办。去年，该展会吸引了逾两万名专业观众与玩家参与，来自13个国家和地区的300多家参展商展示了超过500款优质游戏，行业影响力日益凸显。
背景资料：
莫斯科创意产业局（ACI）是莫斯科市文化局下属的创意产业发展机构，为电子游戏、动画、设计、当代艺术、出版等创意领域的企业与专业人士提供支持，并助力其产品开拓俄罗斯及国际市场。
莫斯科电子游戏与动画集群是推动电子游戏与动画产业发展的专项平台，于2025年11月成立。目前已有 70 余家企业入驻，正在推进的项目超过 250 个。

2

11月21日至22日，第十届独立游戏与游戏文化盛会“WePlay Expo 2026”将在上海国家会展中心盛大举行。在“莫斯科游戏中心”（Moscow Game Hub）展台，中国玩家将有机会亲身体验来自五家莫斯科工作室的12款题材各异的俄罗斯游戏佳作。中国游戏产业界人士也将借此良机，与开发者深入洽谈，探讨新项目在中国的发行策略与市场推广合作。展会期间，俄罗斯企业已安排超过200场商务对接会，合作伙伴涵盖中国主流发行商、渠道分销商及各大游戏平台代表。此次俄罗斯工作室集体亮相WePlay Expo 2026，是首届在华举办的“莫斯科游戏节”的核心组成部分。

俄罗斯是全球独立游戏开发的重要高地之一。据莫斯科创意产业局评估，俄罗斯工作室每年推出约6200款游戏，其中绝大多数为极具创意的独立游戏项目。

本次莫斯科游戏团队赴沪参展，由成立仅一年便汇聚了70余家领军企业、250多个在研精品项目的“莫斯科电子游戏与动画产业集群”精心策划组织。

“参展不仅意味着向广大玩家展示游戏作品，更是拓展商业合作网络的宝贵契机：开发者既能面向发行商、渠道商及游戏平台代表推介项目，又能直接倾听展会观众的真实反馈。目前，已为莫斯科工作室安排了逾200场与中国发行商、渠道商及平台方的商务洽谈。在谈判中，开发者将详细介绍其项目，并深入探讨进入中国市场的前景与策略”莫斯科创意产业局战略发展副局长阿纳斯塔西娅·雷布金娜表示。

此次抵达上海的俄罗斯工作室带来了设定新颖、玩法创新的游戏矩阵，涵盖斯拉夫奇幻、中世纪策略、融合RPG元素的海洋冒险以及多人合作动作类游戏等。例如，WATT Studio展示了动作砍杀游戏《TSAREVNA. Age of Tales》。该作构建了一个阴郁神秘的斯拉夫奇幻世界，其战斗系统更是巧妙融合了古典芭蕾的优雅美学，令人耳目一新。

另一家俄罗斯开发商GEEKY HOUSE则展出了温馨治愈的冒险解谜游戏《Mergewood》，玩家将在游戏中修复祖母留下的家族庄园，重温亲情记忆；此外还有一款像素风角色扮演游戏《MineTap》，主打资源采集与装备打造的深度养成体验。

GEMENOT DIGITAL向展台访客重点介绍了《Feodika》——一款融入国家治理要素的中世纪王朝模拟经营游戏，让玩家体验执掌权柄的策略乐趣。

参展阵容最为庞大的是ANTELUS GAMES，共带来七款风格迥异的作品。其中包括冒险游戏《Heart of Altai》，玩家将跟随女主角探寻失落于阿尔泰秘境的古城；海洋蒸汽朋克题材大作《Sea Walker Saga》，集海盗海战与战斗岛屿建设于一体；以及两款惊悚恐怖游戏：《The Black Ice》，讲述在南极极地设施中的极限求生故事，和《FIRE AND ASHES》，场景设定在一所充满悬疑的精神病院内。该工作室另外三款力作分别为：《The Soul》，讲述猎杀潜伏于人群之中怪物的猎人传奇；多人合作动作游戏《Cat's Wars》，主角是一群手持武器的萌趣猫咪；以及冒险解谜游戏《Always With You: Meow & Mystery》，玩家将与主角一同踏上感人的寻母之旅。

Crumple Studios则为上海玩家带来了《HomeWave》，一个存在于虚拟操作系统内部的独特世界。玩家可以在其中自由布置房间、完成订单任务，并逐步解锁角色背后扣人心弦的故事线。

在展示硬核研发实力的同时，俄罗斯游戏产业界也期待与中国企业在游戏开发、联合发行及全球分销等领域展开深度合作。他们计划在WePlay Expo上与当地发行商、渠道商及平台运营商就项目进入中国市场的具体路径与推广策略进行深入磋商。

WePlay Expo是由中国独立游戏联盟（CiGA）主办的顶级独立游戏与游戏文化行业盛会。2026年，该活动迎来十周年里程碑庆典，继续在上海国家会展中心举办。去年，该展会吸引了逾两万名专业观众与玩家参与，来自13个国家和地区的300多家参展商展示了超过500款优质游戏，行业影响力日益凸显。

 

背景资料：

莫斯科创意产业局（ACI）是莫斯科市文化局下属的创意产业发展机构，为电子游戏、动画、设计、当代艺术、出版等创意领域的企业与专业人士提供支持，并助力其产品开拓俄罗斯及国际市场。

莫斯科电子游戏与动画集群是推动电子游戏与动画产业发展的专项平台，于2025年11月成立。目前已有 70 余家企业入驻，正在推进的项目超过 250 个。
